14	CASE OD2-HO-INTERACT-2 (INTERACT, organizational): Larkspur Community Food Network: regular volunteers drifting away
15	Setting: Larkspur Community Food Network is a fictional regional food-relief nonprofit with four pantry sites (Millbrook, Dock Street, Westgate and Quarry Lane). It relies on about 420 regular volunteers who sort, pack and serve food, including an after-school meals programme for minors at every site. In spring 2026 it introduced a self-scheduling app (RotaWeave) and an annual background-check renewal. After losing a foundation grant, it also eliminated three site coordinator posts. Between March and August the number of active regular volunteers fell sharply, and the board meets on 30 September.
16	Presenting request: The executive director wants an independent view of why regular volunteers have stopped coming and what Larkspur should do. She intends to recommend cancelling the RotaWeave contract at the 30 September board meeting unless the evidence points elsewhere.
17	INITIAL EVIDENCE
18	E1 [stage S1] Mara Ellison, Executive Director, memo to reviewer, 2 September 2026 (leadership-account): Our active regular volunteers fell from 421 in March to 295 in August, the worst drop in our eleven years. I have personally taken about a dozen calls from long-serving volunteers who are furious about RotaWeave, the scheduling app we adopted this spring. At the 30 September board meeting I intend to recommend cancelling the RotaWeave contract and going back to the paper rosters that served us for a decade. One board member also thinks Commonplate Volunteers, a new group that opened on 16 June, is poaching our people. I need an independent view of what happened and what we should do before that meeting.
19	E2 [stage S1] Larkspur project and policy change log (extract) (change-record): RotaWeave rollout plan (approved 12 Feb): Millbrook pilot go-live 3 March; Dock Street, Westgate and Quarry Lane go-live 14 April. Basic tier: next week's shifts released to all volunteers every Thursday at 18:00; three staff admin seats; 3-year term, $38,000; early-termination fee $14,000. Policy change (adopted 20 Jan): annual background-check renewal for all regular volunteers, required by the county after-school meals contract and by our insurer for any shift serving minors. Renewal deadline 30 April; volunteers not renewed are deactivated on 1 May until they complete it.
20	E3 [stage S1] Finance memo to staff, 22 April 2026 (financial-record): After the loss of the Pellham Foundation operating grant ($171,000), the following savings take effect on 1 May. The site coordinator posts at Dock Street, Westgate and Quarry Lane are eliminated (3.0 FTE, $148,000 annualised), and volunteer oversight at those three sites moves to the regional operations manager. The Millbrook coordinator post is kept because the county senior-meals contract funds it separately. The remaining savings come from reduced van leasing. We recognise this places extra load on site lead volunteers and thank them for their flexibility.
21	E4 [stage S1] Email from Tobias Wren, Director of Operations and sponsor of the RotaWeave project, to the Executive Director, 28 August 2026 (manager-account): Mara, before the board blames RotaWeave, look at Millbrook. It has been on the app since March, longer than any other site, and its numbers are fine. The slide starts in May, not April. On 1 May we deactivated 23 regulars who hadn't finished their background-check renewal, and plenty more told me the renewal portal was a nightmare. I think the renewal drove people off whether or not they finished it. Cancelling RotaWeave would cost $14k and throw away the attendance data we've finally got for funders. Tobias
22	E5 [stage S1] Volunteer database, board-pack extract (system-record): Definition: an active regular is a volunteer with 3 or more shifts in the prior 60 days. Org-wide month-end counts: Jan 409, Feb 414, Mar 421, Apr 415, May 384, Jun 345, Jul 315, Aug 295. Renewal deadline: 23 regulars were deactivated on 1 May for an incomplete background-check renewal. Of these, 21 completed it and were reactivated by 31 May; the other 2 have since moved away. Site-level counts are not part of the standard board pack.
23	E6 [stage S1] Volunteer pulse survey summary, February and June 2026 (anonymous-staff-survey): Anonymous link sent to all regulars. Overall satisfaction (1–5): February mean 4.2 (n=236); June mean 3.5 (n=198). The lowest-scoring item in June was 'ease of getting the shifts I want' at 3.0, down from 4.1. Follow-up: 61 June respondents chose to give their names and were matched to activity records. Of those who scored overall satisfaction at 2 or below, 7 of 19 (37%) were inactive by August, against 4 of 42 (10%) of the rest. Site is not recorded.
24	CATALOGUE (full contents)
25	C1 [stage S1] RotaWeave uptime and support-ticket summary, April–August 2026 - RotaWeave customer success team (vendor-account): Platform uptime was 99.8%, with two incidents (14 May and 9 July) of under 40 minutes each, both outside shift-release windows. There were 46 support tickets: 21 password resets, 11 SMS notification settings, 8 export questions and 6 other. No open defects affect booking. Adoption: 92% of active volunteers at live sites logged in at least once in August. Account manager's note: 'Larkspur is one of our smoothest Basic-tier deployments. We'd welcome a conversation about Plus-tier features.'
26	C2 [stage S1] Active regular volunteers by site, monthly, March–August 2026, with each site's go-live and staffing status - Volunteer database extract, run by the data officer (system-record): Active regular = 3+ shifts in the prior 60 days. Columns run March to August. Millbrook (RotaWeave since 3 Mar; coordinator kept): 118, 117, 116, 114, 112, 111. Dock Street (RotaWeave since 14 Apr; coordinator post ended 1 May): 112, 110, 96, 78, 64, 55. Westgate (RotaWeave since 14 Apr; coordinator post ended 1 May): 105, 103, 88, 70, 58, 49. Quarry Lane (coordinator post ended 1 May; RotaWeave not live because the kiosk tablets were never delivered, go-live moved to 6 Oct; the lead volunteer keeps the paper standing roster): 86, 85, 84, 83, 81, 80. The background-check deadline applied in the same way at all four sites.
27	C3 [stage S1] Exit-survey responses from volunteers flagged inactive, May–August 2026 - Automated exit email, responses coded by a volunteer-services intern (document): Sent to 141 volunteers flagged inactive; 13 responded (9%). Reasons, coded from free text: busy/other commitments 4, health 2, moved away 1, 'changes at the pantry' 3, prefer not to say 3. The site field was optional and left blank in 11 responses. Sample comments: 'Just a lot going on this summer.' 'Things changed and it didn't feel the same.' 'Might come back in the autumn.'
28	C4 [stage S1] Background-check provider processing report, January–May 2026 - Verisett Screening account report (vendor-account): Renewal checks submitted: 402. Median turnaround was 3.5 working days, and the 90th percentile was 8 days. 31 applicants were asked to re-upload ID because the image was blurred. Portal availability was 99.5%. The cost is $18 per check, invoiced monthly. Provider's note: 'Submissions peaked in the last ten days before your 30 April deadline, which lengthened median turnaround to 6 days for that fortnight.'
29	C5 [stage S1] Volunteer demographics by site, April 2026 snapshot - Volunteer database extract (system-record): Figures are for regular volunteers in April 2026, listed as Millbrook, Dock Street, Westgate, Quarry Lane. Median age: 63, 62, 64, 61. Share aged 70+: 24%, 22%, 26%, 21%. Median tenure: 4.4, 4.1, 4.6, 3.8 years. Share with a smartphone number on file: 81%, 83%, 79%, 80%. Share referred by a corporate partner: 6%, 9%, 7%, 5%.
30	C6 [stage S1] Interview with the regional operations manager, 3 September 2026 - Imran Castell, Regional Operations Manager (covering Dock Street, Westgate and Quarry Lane since 1 May) (manager-account): 'I can't be at three sites, so I manage from the RotaWeave dashboard. At Dock Street and Westgate the fill rate is above 95% every week, because corporate groups and new sign-ups snap the shifts up, so coverage isn't the problem. Honestly, I think some of the older regulars just didn't want to deal with change, and the renewal paperwork came at the worst possible time. The lead volunteers at each site handle anything day-to-day, and they haven't raised anything urgent with me.'
31	C7 [stage S1] Volunteer services booking reconciliation for Dock Street, Westgate and Millbrook, April–August 2026 - Lucia Brandt, Volunteer Services Manager, compiled from RotaWeave audit logs and callback notes (document): Basic tier has no recurring bookings, so a regular keeps a weekly slot only if staff book it before Thursday's public release. 'Book on behalf' entries: Millbrook 78–84/week throughout; Dock Street plus Westgate 74/week (14–30 Apr) and 3/week since 1 May. One admin seat has been unused since 1 May. Of 213 April regulars at Dock Street/Westgate, 129 lost their usual slot at least twice in May–June, mostly to new or corporate sign-ups; 114 of them (88%) are now inactive, against 9 of 84 (11%) who kept their slot. At Millbrook, 7 of 117 lost their slot. 121 of the 123 who lapsed held a current background check at their last shift. Callbacks reached 61: 44 'lost my regular shift / nobody booked me', 7 health/moving, 5 other commitments, 3 no reason, 2 joined another group.
32	C8 [stage S1] Board minutes, 12 February 2026 (RotaWeave procurement) - Board secretary (document): Item 4: the Director of Operations presented the RotaWeave proposal, comparing three vendors. The board chose the Basic tier on cost ($38,000 over three years, against $61,000 for Plus). Benefits cited: real-time attendance data for funders, fewer no-shows through SMS reminders, and less coordinator time spent rostering by phone. The treasurer asked about the early-termination terms ($14,000). Motion carried 7–1. Item 5: the board noted the background-check renewal policy adopted on 20 January.
33	C9 [stage S1] Commonplate Volunteers public announcements and recruitment posts, June–August 2026 - Public website and social media posts (external-data): Press release, 16 June: Commonplate Volunteers opens a community kitchen on Harlow Street, 0.6 miles from Larkspur's Millbrook site. Its recruitment posts claim '180 volunteers signed up in our first eight weeks'. Roles listed are cooking, delivery driving and front-of-house, on evening and weekend shifts. The posts give no information on where these volunteers previously served.
34	C10 [stage S1] Regional food-bank network volunteer benchmarking, 2025–26 - Regional food-bank network annual survey (external-data): Eleven member organisations took part. Median 6-month retention of regular volunteers was 84% in 2025 and 81% in 2026, with a 2026 range of 72% to 90%. Seven of the 11 respondents cited 'post-pandemic fatigue' or 'cost of living' as pressures. Larkspur did not submit 2026 data. Method: figures are self-reported, and members define 'regular' in different ways.
35	C11 [stage S1] Pulse survey item-level results, February and June 2026 - Volunteer pulse survey, full item report (anonymous-staff-survey): Item means (1–5), February to June: ease of getting the shifts I want 4.1 → 3.0; I feel valued 4.4 → 3.9; communication from staff 4.0 → 3.4; training adequacy 3.9 → 3.8; would recommend volunteering here 4.5 → 3.9. Coded themes in June free text: 'app' 41 mentions, 'great team' 35, 'staff not around' 22, 'renewal process' 18. The site field was not collected.
36	C12 [stage S1] Site coordinator job description and 1 May handover checklist - HR file (document): Job description (2023): 'Recruit, schedule, support and recognise volunteers; maintain site safety and food-handling logs; liaise with partner agencies.' Handover checklist, Dock Street, signed 30 April: keys and alarm codes to the lead volunteer; food-safety logbooks to the lead volunteer; RotaWeave admin login to the regional operations manager; partner agency contacts to the regional operations manager; volunteer birthday and recognition list to the lead volunteer.
37	C13 [stage S1] Monthly food distributed, client visits and volunteer hours, January–August 2026 - Finance and operations dashboard (financial-record): Org-wide food distributed (thousand lb): Jan 212, Feb 205, Mar 219, Apr 224, May 221, Jun 230, Jul 236, Aug 229. Client household visits ranged from 9,800 to 10,600 a month with no trend. Recorded volunteer hours were 6,140 in March and 5,520 in August. Corporate-group volunteer hours rose from 410 in March to 1,180 in August.
38	C14 [stage S1] County after-school meals contract and insurer safeguarding clauses, January 2026 - Contract and insurance file (document): County contract §7.3: 'All persons working shifts at which meals are served to minors must hold a background check completed within the previous 12 months. Non-compliance is grounds for suspension of the contract.' Insurer endorsement to Larkspur's general liability policy: cover for abuse or molestation claims depends on annual screening of every volunteer in contact with minors. After-school meals run at all four sites, Monday to Thursday.
39	C15 [stage S1] Social-media mentions of Larkspur, April–August 2026 - Communications team monitoring tool (external-data): The monitoring tool captured 37 public mentions. 19 were positive (mostly donation drives and a corporate volunteer day), 11 neutral and 7 negative: three about the scheduling app, two about parking at Westgate and two about client wait times. There was no spike in mention volume, and no posts from accounts identifiable as Larkspur volunteers announcing that they were leaving.
40	CANDIDATES
41	H1: The move to app-based self-scheduling, on its own, caused the fall in active regular volunteers.
42	H2: The elimination of site coordinator posts, on its own, caused the fall in active regular volunteers.
43	H3: The fall in active regular volunteers arose from the move to app-based self-scheduling and the elimination of site coordinator posts acting together; neither change on its own produces it.
44	H4: The background-check renewal requirement, on its own, caused the fall in active regular volunteers.
45	H5: Recruitment by the newly opened Commonplate Volunteers, on its own, caused the fall in active regular volunteers.
46	R1: Site coordinator post eliminated at a site using app-based self-scheduling -> Regular volunteers losing their usual weekly shift (causes)
47	R2: Regular volunteers losing their usual weekly shift -> Regular volunteers becoming inactive (causes)
48	R3: Background-check renewal requirement with a 30 April deadline -> Fall in active regular volunteers from May onward (causes)
49	R4: Low volunteer satisfaction score in the June pulse survey -> Regular volunteers becoming inactive (causes)
50	A1: At Dock Street and Westgate, give a staff member or trained lead volunteer a RotaWeave admin seat and the job of booking regulars into their usual weekly slots before each Thursday release. Phone lapsed regulars to offer them their former slot back, and review re-engagement after 60 days.
51	A2: Make a volunteer recognition and appreciation programme the centrepiece of the retention response, on the premise that low satisfaction is what is driving regulars to leave.
52	A3: Suspend the background-check renewal requirement until volunteer numbers recover.
53	A4: Cancel the RotaWeave contract at all four sites, paying the $14,000 early-termination fee, and return to paper rosters.
54	A5: Before the board meeting, remove regulars with no shift in the past 45 days from the volunteer roster and from the retention figures.

answers.justification: Millbrook has run RotaWeave since 3 March with its coordinator kept and stayed flat (118→111, C2), and only 7 of 117 lost their slot there (C7); the vendor data show no booking defects (C1). So the app alone does not produce the fall.
Quarry Lane lost its coordinator on 1 May but kept a paper standing roster, and it stayed nearly flat (86→80, C2). So losing the coordinator alone does not produce the fall.

The fall is confined to Dock Street and Westgate, the only sites with both the app and no coordinator (C2). C7 gives the mechanism: Basic tier has no recurring bookings, book-on-behalf entries collapsed from 74 to 3 a week after 1 May, and 88% of regulars who lost their slot are inactive against 11% who kept it.

The deadline applied equally at all four sites, yet Millbrook and Quarry Lane were stable (C2). 21 of the 23 deactivated volunteers were reactivated by 31 May (E5), and 121 of the 123 who lapsed held a current check at their last shift (C7).
Commonplate opened 0.6 miles from Millbrook, which stayed stable (C9, C2). The slide began in May, before its 16 June opening (E5), and only 2 of 61 callbacks said they had joined another group (C7).

The order of events, the mechanism and a contrast all line up. Basic tier has no recurring bookings, staff book-on-behalf entries fell from 74 to 3 a week after the coordinator posts ended, and 129 of 213 regulars at Dock Street/Westgate lost their slot against 7 of 117 at Millbrook, which had the app and kept its coordinator (C7, E2, E3, C2).

88% of regulars who lost their slot became inactive against 11% who kept it, and 44 of 61 callbacks named losing the regular shift. Sites where slots were kept stayed stable (C7, C2), though there is no randomised or intervention evidence yet.
The deadline was uniform across sites, but only the two sites with both changes fell (C2). Almost all deactivated volunteers were reactivated (E5), and almost all who lapsed held current checks (C7).

Low scorers were more often inactive (37% vs 10%, E6), but the sample is small and self-selected, and the item that fell most was 'ease of getting the shifts I want' (C11). That suggests low satisfaction is a symptom of losing slots rather than an independent cause.

This restores the missing book-on-behalf function in the way Millbrook's coordinator does it (C7), using the unused admin seat. It targets the mechanism identified in C2 and C7 and has a built-in 60-day review.
The premise rests on R4, which is only an association (E6, C11). Recognition does not address the lost weekly slots that drive the lapses (C7).

Annual checks are required by the county contract and the insurer for shifts serving minors at every site (C14). The requirement is not the cause of the fall (C2, C7), so suspending it would disable a protective control.

The app alone is not the cause (Millbrook, C2/C7), so cancelling costs a $14,000 fee (E2) and throws away the attendance data used for funders (E4, C8). It blames the wrong factor when cheaper targeted fixes exist.
Removing lapsed regulars before the board meeting would hide the retention loss shown in E5 and C2. It would also drop exactly the people A1 aims to win back (C7), which suppresses information.
The site contrasts in C2, the slot-loss mechanism and callbacks in C7, and the vendor and demographic data ruling out rivals (C1, C5) are enough to commit to A1, a low-cost and reversible fix.

ambiguousItems: Q13: A4 could be read as 'acceptable', since paper standing rosters kept Quarry Lane stable and would restore regulars' slots. It could also be read as 'premature' rather than 'harmful'. I chose harmful because H1 is contradicted and cancelling has real costs ($14k fee, lost funder data).

Q7: R2 could be read as 'association-only', because the comparison of lost-slot and kept-slot regulars is observational and could be confounded by commitment level. The callbacks and the site contrast favour causal.
Q11: A2 could be read as 'acceptable' as a cheap add-on, rather than 'premature'.
caseProblems: C7 is unusually decisive: one compiled document holds the mechanism, the rate contrast, the rule-out of the background-check rival, and callback reasons. That makes the case close to a single-item solve.
The title of C2 ('with each site's go-live and staffing status') signals that it sets up the interaction contrast, which leaks the analytical frame somewhat.
Internal consistency checks out: site counts in C2 add up to the org-wide totals in E5 for every month, and 110+103=213 matches the April Dock Street/Westgate regulars in C7.
Minor point: 123 lapsed (C7) against a net drop of about 113 at Dock Street/Westgate (C2) implies some new regulars arrived. That is plausible but not stated.
